News.title: Cop reveals true story of Narcos’ Cali drug empire after exposing cartel where gangs set death squads on own people
News.content:
NOT ALL WHITE Cop reveals true story of Narcos’ Cali drug empire after exposing cartel where gangs set death squads on own people

CHRIS Feistl kneels behind rows of cocaine bags in a cargo container, dressed in a white vest and blue shorts.

It’s an unusual image, because with long, surfer-style blonde hair, he doesn’t look like someone you would expect to be posing near a huge stash of the world’s most notorious Class A drug.





But Feistl was a top DEA agent who had just wrestled 250g of the addictive white powder off Colombia’s most notorious drug gangs, the Cali Cartel.

His career was portrayed by Michael Stahl-David in hit Netflix show, Narcos, along with DEA partner, Dave Mitchell.

Feistl was first moved to Bogota in 1994, from Miami, just one year after the death of infamous drug lord Pablo Escobar, exploding the country into a tinderbox of violence.

He told The Sun: “When I got to Colombia, it was the major leagues and it was a crazy time to be involved.”

The Mecca of drug trafficking, Colombia led the world in kidnappings and murders when Feistl arrived, making it the world’s most dangerous country.

His job was to take down the cartel’s four leaders, known as the Cali Godfathers: Gilberto Rodriguez Orejuela, his younger brother, Miguel Rodríguez Orejuela, Jose Santacruz Londono and Helmer Herrera.

Together they ran the cartel for almost two decades.



Feistl said: “They were bringing cocoa paste and different stuff from Peru and Bolivia into Colombia, but then Gilberto decided they needed to get involved in cocaine because that is where the future was at.

“Gilberto was called the chess player as he was always thinking two or three steps ahead, and he nailed this one, because their future really did lie in cocaine.”

To take them down, Feistl and Mitchell embedded themselves into the Colombian National Police and were assigned to a Search Bloc, a special operations unit, targeting the cartels.

Soon they were doing daily raids but quickly learned about the force’s crippling corruption culture.

Feistl said: “Corruption was so systemic in that Search Bloc that we had to start working on our own.



“We had to get away from the police base we were staying at and move to a safe house.

“We realised how infiltrated with spies that Search Bloc was so in order to be effective, we had to start working with specially vetted teams.

“They were polygraphed police units trained in the US, they were drug tested and went through extensive background screening.

“But the DEA didn’t have their own vetted unit at the time, so what we had to do was work with a vetted unit attached to the CIA.”

With vetted officers, Feistl and Mitchell were able to fully set their sights on their first takedown, Gilberto, after a year on the ground.



To get to the kingpin they needed to recruit sources within the cartel who were motivated by money or safety, exchanging information for security.

He said: “We had two sources who gave us very specific information about one of Gilberto’s executive assistants.



“The information was that if you follow him, he will lead you to Gilberto, because he goes to Gilberto’s house every day.

“So we were able to surveil this guy.”

In just a week Feistl and his team had raided the residence and arrested Gilberto.

Feistl said: “The DEA has always been very renowned for cultivating assets, confidential informants, and during that time Dave and I were on the ground continually recruiting assets and evaluating the information.

“One of the key things we pushed for in Colombia was to have rewards for the capture of these kingpins and it wasn’t until 1995 that they finally put these rewards out for the capture of the four Cali cartel leaders.”



Rewards of $1,875million (£1.415m) were offered up for the capture of Miguel and Gilberto, the two principal leaders, while information leading to the arrest of Jose and Helmer came in at $625,000 (£467,162).

They were advertised on TV, in the newspapers and on the radio every day.

Feistl said: “That’s how we brought a lot of sources to the table.

“We were able to develop information from one source who happened to be from Ecuador, who was part of the cartel, and another in Colombia, looking for their rewards.

“Many were also targeted by the Cali cartel, so we knew they were going to be killed and obviously that’s a good way to get in.



“We could say we can offer you protection if you provide information.”

But life in Colombia came at a price for Feistl, who was constantly wary of his safety.

For a start, he was easily identifiable as an American, with long, blonde hair running down his back.

While Dave was 6ft 3ins and built like “an NFL tight end”.

“Our lives felt in danger all the time. We were immediately picked out as DEA or CIA operatives,” Feistl said.



Operations were carried out at night, after sun down, when the pair would meet assets after carrying out surveillance detection routes.

Feistl said: “We were followed a lot by the cartel.

“They would pick us up on surveillance, or if we ever left a police base, the corrupt officials assigned to the Search Bloc would call and say ‘hey, gringos are leaving’, and they would wait for us.

“We would have to traverse down a one-way street for a mile or two into this huge traffic circle and the Cali Cartel would always set up surveillance assets in that traffic circle, because we had to pass by it.



“They knew that any kind of operation we would do had to involve the military or police, and they had that covered because they had all their spies there.

“The minute we did anything, they would call them and say hey, the DEA is doing an operation, and it would be compromised.

“But the biggest threat to the cartel at the time was the informants, so they would try to follow us to identify them.



“If they were successful and saw us meeting with someone, they would immediately kill those guys.”

The duo believed the cartel would leave them unharmed because of the cautionary tale of Kiki Camarena, a DEA agent murdered in Mexico, and the blowback that followed.

But there were still occasions they thought they may never return home.

He said: “Once we met with a high-level asset, the head of security for the cartel, in a sugar cane field about an hour outside Cali.

“Unfortunately a taxi cab driver had his car robbed and there was a huge police presence in a very isolated area.



“Police stumbled upon us and we could not identify ourselves because we had to protect our source, so we threw our weapons away into the sugar cane field, and our IDs. But they had us at gunpoint, interrogating us.

“Finally, we bribed our way out. We had to give the police officers money.

“That was five days before we took down Miguel with that asset’s help.”

Eventually, Londono surrendered before an arrest at a restaurant, while Herrera also surrendered.

News.title: Boy, 17, among two more arrested over ‘murder’ of pedestrian, 45, hit by car as woman & two men also held
News.content:
CRASH 'MURDER' Boy, 17, among two more arrested over ‘murder’ of pedestrian, 45, hit by car as woman & two men also held

A TEEN boy is among two more suspects arrested after a horror smash left a 45-year-old man dead.

Cops swooped following the fatal incident involving a pedestrian and a white Volkswagen in Barnsley on Friday afternoon.





The victim tragically died at the scene despite emergency services rushing to help.

Today, a 33-year-old man and a 17-year-old boy were arrested on suspicion of murder and remain in police custody.

Officers had already arrested two others over the shocking incident.

A 60-year-old man and a 38-year-old woman were arrested yesterday – both also on suspicion of murder.



Cops were first called by the ambulance service after reports of the crash.

The victim’s heartbroken family are being supported by specially trained officers as investigations continue.

A police cordon that sealed Rose Tree Avenue following the incident has now been lifted.

Speaking following the tragedy, Detective Chief Inspector Simon Cartwright said the probe is in its early stages.



“Our thoughts first and foremost are with the victim’s family, friends and loved ones,” he said.

“Detectives are working hard to piece together the circumstances of what happened and we would urge anyone with information to please get in touch with us.

“Officers will remain in Rose Tree Avenue carrying out further enquiries.

“If you have any concerns, queries or information you wish to share then please speak to our officers while they are in the area.”

A spokesperson for the force added: “We are continuing to work at pace to understand the circumstances of this incident and are asking for anyone with information which could assist officers with their enquiries to come forward.”



Anyone with information is asked to get in touch with cops, quoting incident number 689 of 3 April 2026.

News.title: UK weather: Storm Dave lashes Britain with 93mph winds as ‘heavy & widespread’ showers to cause more travel misery today
News.content:
DISMAL DAVE UK weather: Storm Dave lashes Britain with 93mph winds as ‘heavy & widespread’ showers to cause more travel misery today

BRITS are bracing for more Storm Dave misery as “widespread downpours” are forecast to hit Britain today.

Strong winds hit 93mph yesterday with temperatures plummeting to -3C – causing travel chaos across much of the UK.





And the Easter weather woes will continue today as flood warnings are in place across parts of the country.

Yesterday, the Met Office upgraded a severe yellow weather warning for wind to amber, meaning flying debris could lead to “injuries or danger to life”.

This primarily affected the north of the UK, with amber wind alerts in place across northern England, north-west Wales and southern Scotland which was lifted at 3am this morning.

Wales was also under a yellow wind alert, but this was lifted at 7am this morning.

Following “severe gales” and winds of up to 93mph, roads were closed and train services disrupted early this morning.

Traffic Scotland warned that several major bridges had restrictions in place due to the strong winds, including the Queensferry Crossing on the M90, which connects Edinburgh with Fife and the nearby Forth Road Bridge on the A9000.



The Humber Bridge linking East Yorkshire with north Lincolnshire reopened after being closed in both directions to high-sided and vulnerable vehicles early on Sunday due to strong winds, National Highways reported.

Elsewhere, ScotRail confirmed emergency speed restrictions would be implemented across parts of its network, resulting in longer travel times.

In England’s north, Network Rail Manchester announced rail replacement bus services would run between Manchester Picadilly and Chester due to overnight weather conditions.

The forecast is expected to clear up throughout today, but two yellow wind alerts remain in place until noon for parts of northern England and Scotland.

The Met Office’s forecast for Easter Sunday said: “Storm Dave will clear northeast on Sunday morning, leaving sunshine and widespread showers across the UK.



“Northern areas will see the heaviest, blustery showers and feel cold, while temperatures elsewhere stay closer to average for early April.”

As of 7am today, there were four coastal flood warnings and 32 flood alerts across England and eight coastal flood alerts in Wales.



In Scotland, 12 flood warnings and eight flood alerts remained in place.

The Energy Networks Association, which represents electricity network operators, warned of potential power cuts and issued safety advice following the weather warnings.

It said in a statement on Saturday: “The storm has the potential to affect local power infrastructure, increasing the risk of a power cut and fallen power lines.

“Network operators are increasing staffing for operational teams, and moving spare equipment to where the weather is expected to be most disruptive, so it’s ready to use if needed.”



As the Easter bank holiday continues, Storm Dave will move into the North Sea which will ease weather conditions today.

Rain and wind will continue across Scotland and Northern Ireland, but most of England and Wales will enjoy more settled weather.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

On Easter Monday there will be dry conditions thanks to a ridge of high pressure bringing sunny spells to most areas after a chilly Sunday night.

Next week will likely see warmer weather before more unsettled conditions return in the midweek, with cloud and rain likely to come in from the west.

News.title: Top CEO killed and son, 11, injured in horror crash on dream family holiday as tributes paid to ‘brilliant’ mother
News.content:
TRAGIC END Top CEO killed and son, 11, injured in horror crash on dream family holiday as tributes paid to ‘brilliant’ mother

A TOP CEO has been killed in a horror crash while on a dream family holiday which also left her son, 11, injured.

Tributes have poured in for Kasey Grelle, 41, who died after an open-air tourist transport truck crashed in Tola, Nicaragua.





The mom-of-three was the co-founder of the St. Louis-based marketing consulting firm Aux Insights in Missouri.

Her oldest son Julian was critically injured in the smash and was airlifted back to the US, according to a family fundraiser.

His family shared that he suffered head trauma, skull fractures and spine fractures as well as a collapsed lung,

Grelle, was one of about 30 people – including children – to be in the tour truck when it lost control within the Rancho Santana resort on March 23, according to local media reports.

read more world news PARADE HORROR At least 15 injured as car ploughs into crowd during parade as driver charged



It’s understood the truck was travelling down a hill when it rolled.

She was rushed to hospital by first responders but sadly died on the way.

Grelle reportedly suffered catastrophic injuries, including severe head trauma and a skull fracture.

Her brother Andy Joyce shared the tragic news on Facebook, remembering his sister as, “one of the most brilliant, driven and selfless people I have ever met.”



“She was relentless in everything she did, especially when it came to helping people.”

Grelle is survived by her husband, Dave, and their three young children — Julian, 11; Kit, 9; and Des, 6.

A GoFundMe crowdfunding effort launched to benefit the children has raised more than $302,000 as of Saturday — well past the initial $250,000 goal.

Nicaragua’s National Police are still investigating the circumstances of the crash.

In a 2025 podcast interview, Grelle said Aux Insight had surpassed $10 million in annual revenue in under two years and was profitable from the outset without outside funding, as reported by the New York Times.



Before launching Aux Insights, Grelle worked in venture capital and corporate dealmaking, including a stint as CEO of Gateway Media.

She began her career as a TV news reporter before pivoting into finance and entrepreneurship after earning an MBA from Washington University in St. Louis.

News.title: Lucy Letby ‘terrified she’s top target for murder by savage inmates in jail after Ian Huntley & Ian Watkins deaths’
News.content:
BABY killer Lucy Letby fears she could be murdered in jail after fiends Ian Huntley and Ian Watkins were savagely attacked and killed behind bars.

Letby, 36 – serving 15 whole-life sentences for murdering seven babies – is currently being held in a secure unit at HMP Bronzefield in Surrey.





The sickening death toll saw her become the UK’s most prolific killer nurse and one of Britain’s worst-ever female serial killers.

Notorious lags Watkins and Huntley were both killed after being targeted by other inmates in their high-security prisons.

Letby, in custody since 2020, is on a unit alongside baby killer aristocrat Constance Marten and Sara Sharif’s stepmum Beinash Batool.

And sources say that despite having a “number of supporters” in the prison, Letby now fears she could be next.

One told the Daily Star: “Lucy is frightened that she could be attacked and killed by one of the inmates inside HMP Bronzefield.

“She knows that other high-profile prisoners have been attacked and killed recently… this is something that worries her.

“There are some very dangerous women in Bronzefield and they would see any attack on her as increasing their status within the jail.”



Huntley, serving life for the murders of ten-year-olds Holly Wells and Jessica Chapman, died last month after being savagely attacked in jail.

The Soham monster was battered to death in a workshop inside top-security Frankland jail in County Durham last month.

Huntley – left in an induced coma – died aged 52 after doctors turned off his life support after consulting his mother.

Meanwhile, last October, paedo rockstar Watkins was ambushed after cons were unlocked from their cells at Wakefield Prison in West Yorkshire.

Watkins, 48, was serving 35 years for a string of child sex offences, including the attempted rape of a baby.



The ex-Lostprophets frontman – who narrowly survived previous assaults by inmates – died from blood loss after having his jugular slashed.

We previously revealed how Letby was being monitored around the clock after being mocked by lags over the Netflix documentary on her case.

The Investigation of Lucy Letby explores both sides of the divisive case behind the UK’s most prolific killer nurse.

Prison staff have been told to check her every hour and speak to her for at least ten minutes a day to assess her over suicide fears.



Officers at the prison began an assessment, care in custody and teamwork process to contain fallout over the 90-minute programme.

Inmates cannot watch Netflix in the jail but are in phone contact with people outside.

Our source said: “They also get newspapers and it’s likely there are some smartphones inside… so some of the girls might even have seen it.”

Letby has also had extra safety checks because of taunts over her controversial case.

She carried out her sick crimes in a year-long spree at Countess of Chester Hospital, using insulin and air to inject newborns on the neo-natal ward.



The collapses and deaths of the children were not “naturally-occurring tragedies” and instead the gruesome work of “poisoner” Letby.

Her rampage was finally uncovered after staff grew suspicious of the rise in the number of babies dying or suffering “catastrophic” collapses.

After a harrowing nine-month trial in August 2023, Letby was found guilty of murdering seven babies and the attempted murder of six others.

Verdicts could not be reached on six counts of attempted murder, but after 22 days of jury deliberation, she was handed 14 whole-life sentences.

The following year, Letby was found guilty of the attempted murder of Child K and given another whole-life order after a retrial.

She lost two bids in 2024 to challenge her convictions.

But the Criminal Cases Review Commission is now considering evidence claiming natural causes and poor care caused the deaths.

News.title: China’s apocalyptic ghost towns of rotting mansions where 65MILLION homes lie deserted as Communist rulers face chaos
News.content:
ACROSS China, vast cities of silent high-rises stretch across the horizon – empty, unfinished, and uninhabited.

These so-called “ghost cities” are haunting reminders of the country’s breakneck economic rise over the last 30 years – and the bumpy landing that followed.





No country has ever built so much so quickly and it means ghost cities – also known as metropolises that have yet to come to life – lie in every corner of China.

Dozens of skyscrapers pop up overnight and chilling pictures show the vacant – and sometimes half-finished structures – which have been deserted by developers.

Rows of post-apocalyptic housing estates tower over visitors – and impressive attractions and shopping malls gather dust without any residents or tourists stepping foot inside.

Built on a mountain of debt, Gulcin Ozkan, from King’s Business School, told The Sun that China’s property “downturn” has sparked “significant turmoil”.

“The shock is large for China,” she says.

According to Insider, around 65 million homes stood empty in China in 2020 – enough to house the entire population of France.

Despite the eerie silence, almost all of the homes are owned.



Many were never meant to be lived in. Instead, investors bought these properties as a store of wealth.

“When 70 per cent of household wealth is tied up in property, as in China, the entire economy becomes exceptionally vulnerable to the housing market,” Ozkan says.

The story of China’s ghost cities began in the late 1990s, when Beijing deregulated housing.

State-owned land was sold off, and local officials discovered large-scale construction was the fastest way to boost growth figures.

Farmland was rapidly transformed into vast new towns, built at astonishing speed.



With few alternatives for investing, people poured their savings into real estate as a foolproof way of investing their cash and making a profit.

They also snapped up the properties for their future spouses, kids and grandchildren, or as a retirement pot.

Real estate became the backbone of middle-class wealth.

This is why nearly all the properties in ghost cities are owned – but no one lives there, and some homeowners might never live there.

Max Woodworth, an expert in Chinese urbanisation, said developers and buyers have “tremendous faith” that the value of their property will steadily creep up – and prices won’t crash.



He told The Sun: “Even people who purchased homes in so-called ghost cities, in my experience, rarely express regrets.

“They have come to believe time is on their side and these cities will fill out over time and keep the home values steadily rising.”

Michael Pettis, professor of finance at Peking University, said everyone in China, including developers, had “made the same bet” on exponentially rising property prices.

He told The Guardian: “The problem of course is if property prices ever stop rising, because everyone has made the same bet everyone’s balance sheet starts unravelling at the same time, and it immediately becomes a systemic problem.

“That is what has happened in China.”



Governments also get massive sales revenue from leasing the land out to developers.

“It remains a cornerstone of local economies,” Woodworth said.

“The land system in China produces strong incentives for city governments to promote real estate and land development as a way to raise to revenue and generate economic growth.”

Developers raced ahead, selling homes before they were even built.



For years, the speculative cycle helped drive China’s growth, with real estate accounting for nearly 30 per cent of GDP.

Then Beijing slammed on the brakes. Tighter rules on borrowing and speculation meant the model began to unravel.

Pre-sales dried up, demand plummeted, and construction screeched to a halt.



Prices crashed, leaving half-finished buildings and bankrupt developers in their wake.

The collapse of Evergrande – once China’s biggest developer – became the symbol of the crash.

Buried under $300billion in debt, it left 1.5million unfinished homes and dozens of stalled construction sites nationwide.

Roger Garside, Associate Fellow at the Henry Jackson Society, previously told The Sun that China is facing a “debt mountain”.

Mr Garside said: “The Communist regime has known full well for over a decade the risks that have been building in its economy.



“Its return on investment has been steadily declining. More and more of its economic activity has been unprofitable.”

The Collapse of Evergrande Evergrande was once China’s biggest real estate giant, built on rapid expansion and heavy borrowing.

By 2021, it had accumulated more than $300 bn in debt.

Its business relied on pre-selling apartments and using that cash to fund new projects.

Trouble began when China introduced borrowing limits.

As sales slowed and funding dried up, Evergrande struggled to repay creditors.

It missed key payments in 2021, triggering a default that sent shockwaves through global markets.

The collapse exposed wider weaknesses in China’s property market, with multiple developers being sucked into the crisis.

Millions of homebuyers were left waiting on unfinished properties.

After failed restructuring attempts, a Hong Kong court ordered Evergrande’s liquidation in 2024.

In cities like Ordos, Tianducheng, and Chenggong, vast neighbourhoods of empty streets tell the story.

Ordos was built for one million residents – by 2016, just 100,000 had arrived.

Tianducheng, outside Hangzhou, was meant to be China’s version of Paris.

Complete with a scale replica of the Eiffel Tower and fountains inspired by the Luxembourg Gardens, few residents ever arrived.



Today, its plazas are more often filled with day-trippers posing for photos than people who call it home.

In Chenggong, years of inactivity forced authorities to relocate universities there in a bid to breathe life into its deserted districts.

Elsewhere, projects simply collapsed.

In 2021, 15 skyscrapers in the Sunshine City II complex were demolished after standing unfinished for seven years.

The developer reportedly ran out of cash back in 2013.



Worryingly, China’s property woes go beyond empty buildings.

Unpaid wages and undelivered homes have sparked fears of unrest.



The central bank has promised to protect buyers and inject more cash into the system, but confidence remains shaky.

Ozkan warns the bigger risk may be economic drag rather than financial contagion.

A sharp slowdown in domestic spending could weaken global growth – and new demographic realities are making matters worse.

“China developed new districts on the assumption of endless population and urbanisation growth,” Ozkan says.

Falling birth rates, a shrinking workforce, and slower migration mean the demand needed to fill them “is no longer assured”.



This has left a lasting housing oversupply, weaker prices, and strained local government finances that once depended heavily on land sales.

Writer Wade Shepard first noted the nation’s ghost cities in the early 2000s after making a wrong turn at a bus station in Tianti, Zhejiang and finding miles of empty high-rises.

However, some once-empty cities have begun to come to life.

Dantu, in Zhenjiang, struggled for years but slowly began filling up from 2013.

It now has around 286,000 residents.



Even Tianducheng’s population tripled by 2017.

Pudong, once mocked as a ghost district, is now Shanghai’s thriving financial centre with more than 5.6 million residents.

New projects like Xiong’an – Xi Jinping’s flagship “smart city” – show both the ambition and the risks of China’s urban vision.

Still unfinished, it already houses over a million people. a sign patience may be key to understanding the ghost city phenomenon.

Ultimately, China must change its course.



“The country now needs growth driven by productivity, innovation, services, and consumption,” Ozkan says.

This is an especially difficult transition when household wealth in locked away in property and confidence is fragile.

As for fears families could lose everything, Ozkan says: “The government is likely to do almost anything necessary to avoid this scenario. A complete wipeout of savings is unlikely.”

Critics argue these towns were victims of overdevelopment and poor planning.

Between 1984 and 2010, China’s urban land grew five-fold.



From 2011 to 2013, the country used more concrete than the United States did in the entire 20th century.

Inevitably, construction outpaced demand.

Now, as China’s population begins to shrink for the first time in decades, the question is no longer how to build – but how to fill what’s already there.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Whether these empty skylines will become thriving communities or permanent warnings remains unclear.

For now, China’s ghost cities stand as towering reminders of both the promise – and the peril – of growth at all costs.

News.title: Gunfire exchanged in daring special ops raid as US rescues downed pilot in Iran – but is forced to blow up own planes
News.content:
THE second American pilot missing after Iran shot down a US fighter jet has been rescued under heavy fire in a daring dawn raid

Elite special operations troops were forced to blow up their own planes as they extracted the stricken crew member during a dangerous mission deep within enemy territory.





Donald Trump hailed it as “one of the most daring Search and Rescue Operations in US History”.

Elite forces faced a race against the clock to retrieve two servicemen stranded in the Iranian hinterland after their £60m F-15 was hit by Iranian air defences on Friday.



Both the weapons systems officer (WSO), who sits behind the pilot and is also known as the backseater, and the pilot were forced to eject over region’s in the country’s southwest.

The pilot was rescued quickly, but his colleague, a Colonel, could not immediately be located.

Armed only with a handgun and struggling with a leg injury he climbed up a 7,000ft mountain ridge before hiding in a crevice to evade local tribesmen wielding AK47s.

State TV had earlier offered a £50,000 reward to anyone who could return the stricken airman alive.



Footage on Iranian social media shows the men patrolling the mountains and waving Iranian flags, with one telling the camera: “Don’t worry, we will find them, God willing.”

As he put his Survival, Evasion, Resistance, and Escape (SERE) training into practice, CIA spooks launched their deception campaign, utilising local contacts and other methods to spread the word that the flier had already been found and was being evacuated out of Iran in a ground convoy.

They also contacted locals they hoped might assist in a province which in parts is less supportive of the regime, a tactic known as “unconventional assisted recovery.”

Meanwhile, Special Forces led by America’s dedicated Search and Rescue force, the Parerescuemen, were fine-tuning the last details of their receovry op once they had a confirmed location for the WSO.

The CIA eventually pinpointed his location, passed it to the Pentagon and the incredible operation worthy of a Hollywood thriller swung into action.



It has yet to be revealed, but the two possible provinces – Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad, and Khuzestan – were offered as the site of the downed jet.

Israel assisted by launching a huge blitz of more than 120 targets, effectively laying down a vast carpet of covering fire.

American troops did the same, dropping bombs and opening fire on Iranian military convoys to clear the way for “one of the most challenging and complex missions in the history of US special operations”.

A series of Special Forces teams on HH-60W Jolly Green II helicopters flew to the confirmed target location including commandos from Navy SEAL Team 6, the legendary unit which killed Osama Bin Laden in 2011.

They landed briefly and confirmed the WSO’s identity, a process that likely included at least one question based on information in his Isolated Personnel Report (ISOPREP) that only he would know the answer to.



The document, held by the intelligence section of his unit, contains photographs, fingerprints and personal info and was passed to those coordinating his rescue to allow that final ID to be carried out.

Once it was confirmed he was taken aboard the chopper and was flown to Kuwait for medical treatment.



But in a final, heart stopping twist, two transport planes taking part in the op got stuck in sand at a remote air base in Iran.

Three other planes had to be scrambled to rescue the crews and Special Forces soldiers then destroyed the stranded aircraft to prevent sensitive info falling into Iranian hands.

Two US military planes were destroyed in the aftermath of the raid to prevent the regime getting its hands on sensitive tech, a source told the the Wall Street Journal.

Trump later announced to the world that the missing Colonel had been successfully extracted, sharing that he had been injured but will be “just fine”, adding that he took refuge on the treacherous mountains of Iran.

In a triumphant Truth Social post, Trump wrote: “WE GOT HIM!



“My fellow Americans, over the past several hours, the United States Military pulled off one of the most daring Search and Rescue Operations in U.S. History, for one of our incredible Crew Member Officers, who also happens to be a highly respected Colonel, and who I am thrilled to let you know is now SAFE and SOUND!

“At my direction, the U.S. Military sent dozens of aircraft, armed with the most lethal weapons in the World, to retrieve him.”

Washington had been desperate to retrieve the two servicemen before they came into the clutches of the bloodthirsty IRGC.

Inside elite unit who raced to rescue the US pilot by Robin Perrie, Chief Foreign Correspondent THE search for the missing American pilot was spearheaded by one of the world’s most highly trained Special Forces units dubbed the PJs. The pararescuemen – whose entire focus is Personnel Recovery (PR) – have an incredible range of skills including parachuting from 30,000ft, rescuing soldiers trapped underground and conducting life-saving medical procedures while under enemy fire. These units are often pre-emptively deployed near war zones where aircraft could be taken out. Top brass came to realise the need for a dedicated rescue force during the Second World War and the Pararescue Unit was established in 1946 with the motto “These Things We Do, That Others May Live”. The nickname derives from early flight logs when they were entered as PJ, a combination of Parachutist and Jumper. The unit comprises around 500 special operators who work as independent teams whenever an American or allied soldier needs rescuing. Security analyst Aaron MacLean, a Marine Corps veteran, said: “They are an extraordinary group of special operators.” Their nickname derives from early flight logs when they were entered as PJ, a combination of Parachutist and Jumper. The unit comprises around 500 special operators who work as independent teams whenever an American or allied soldier needs rescuing. READ MORE HERE

The F-15 fighter was the first to have been shot down over enemy territory since the conflict started six weekd ago.



US Central Command immediately launched a desperate search effort – deploying Black Hawks and a low-flying refuelling plane, which were filmed flying low over Khuzestan province.

One airman was swiftly rescued, but the two helicopters involved were pounded by light weaponry as they made their escape.

They returned safely to Iraqi territory, despite one trailing smoke from the damage.

Iranian officials had called on citizens to help locate the remaining American, hoping to gain leverage against Washington.

Broadcasts also showed Iran’s ⁠Revolutionary Guard Corps combing through the area of a search mission.



But Trump celebrated the high-stakes recovery mission, writing: “WE WILL NEVER LEAVE AN AMERICAN WARFIGHTER BEHIND!

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The fact that we were able to pull off both of these operations, without a SINGLE American killed, or even wounded, just proves once again, that we have achieved overwhelming Air Dominance and Superiority over the Iranian skies.

News.title: Brit caught ‘smuggling 1kg of heroin from Thailand’ after scanners spot drugs hidden INSIDE his body
News.content:
LEFT RED-FACED Brit caught ‘smuggling 1kg of heroin from Thailand’ after scanners spot drugs hidden INSIDE his body

A BRIT has been busted in an international airport allegedly attempting to smuggle one kilo of heroin inside his own body.

Ifeanyl Ezeiru-Maru, 52, is facing two serious drug charges after he tried to take the illicit substance into Australia.





Eagle-eyed border patrol officers picked him out for a search in Melbourne Airport on March 22 after he got off a flight from Bangkok.

The Australian Federal Police (AFP) took Ezeiru-Maru to a Melbourne hospital for further assessment.

Medical scans allegedly revealed multiple pellets lurking inside his stomach.

Police have since alleged Ezeiru-Maru was trafficking more than 90 heroin-filled packages of heroin, using his body as the bag.

They were later excreted under medical supervision.

Investigators allege the stash weighed a massive 1.1kg.

Ezeiru-Maru was charged with one count of importing a marketable quantity of a border-controlled drug and one count of possessing a marketable quantity of a border-controlled drug.

Both charges carry a maximum penalty of 25 years in prison or a £835,570 ($1.6 million AUD) fine each.



He remains in police custody and will appear in Melbourne Magistrates’ Court on June 17.

The 1.1kg of heroin has an estimated street value of between £272,500 and £273,500 ($523,000 and $550,000 AUD).

Australian authorities have slammed ruthless drug gangs who treat human couriers as “disposable”.

“Transporting drugs internally is extremely dangerous. Even if only one pellet ruptures, it can be fatal,” Acting Commander Simone Butcher said.

“Criminal syndicates treat couriers as disposable.



“They show no regard for the person’s life or the harm these drugs cause in the community,” she added.

“The AFP, working closely with the Australia Border Force (ABF), will continue to detect and disrupt attempts to import illicit substances, no matter how they are concealed.”

Commander Clinton Sims from the ABF also spoke to the media.

He noted that acting as a drug courier carried not just legal risks, but significant health risks too.

“ABF has advanced, intelligence-led, screening techniques, including working with our international law enforcement partners, to identify travellers who may pose a risk to the Australian community,” he said.



“Our officers are trained to examine more than just baggage, we consider the demeanour and behaviour of travellers, and how they respond to questioning.

“ABF officers are alert to the concealment methods of criminals and have the knowledge and intel before you even step off the plane.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The investigation is ongoing as forensic tests on the drugs are carried out.

News.title: Manchester clubber dies in city centre street moments after leaving venue
News.content:
Manchester clubber dies in city centre street moments after leaving venue

The man, aged in his 20s, died in the street moments after he left a nightclub in Manchester city centre and fell unconscious, with paramedics called to the scene in the early hours

View Image The man died on Portland Street in Manchester (Image: Google Maps)

A man fell ill and died on a street in Manchester city centre just moments after leaving a nightclub.

‌



The man, aged in his 20s, is thought to have suffered a medical episode and fell unconscious in the early hours of Saturday.

‌



Emergency services were called at around 5.45am, but despite their best efforts to revive the man, he was pronounced dead at the scene. Police say there are no suspicious circumstances surrounding his death.

‌



Staff at a nearby nightclub are understood to have helped the man leave the venue shortly before closing time as he was feeling unwell. They then checked on him just before he died, reports Manchester Evening News.

A Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said: "Officers responded to reports of a concern for welfare on Portland Street at around 5.45am yesterday.

Article continues below

"Upon their arrival, officers found a man aged in his 20s unconscious, and despite the best efforts of emergency services, he was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.

"There are believed to be no suspicious circumstances surrounding his death."

News.title: Donald Trump's health scares in full as White House slams 'hospital conspiracy theory'
News.content:
Donald Trump's health scares in full as White House slams 'hospital conspiracy theory'

The White House has been forced to deny 'conspiracy theories' claiming Donald Trump has been rushed to hospital - but it's not the first time rumours have spread about his health in his second term

View 8 Images The White House has issued a new statement on Donald Trump's health (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Donald Trump's health scares have come back into focus after the White House was forced to deny rumours that he was rushed to hospital.

‌



The official 'Rapid Response 47' X account issued a series of fierce denials last night after rumours circulated on social media that Trump was rushed to Walter Reed Medical Centre in Washington DC. One tweet read: "Deranged liberals cook up insane conspiracy theories when @POTUS goes 12 hours without speaking to press. (They said nothing when Biden routinely went 12 days without speaking to press) Fear not! President Trump literally never stops working."

‌



But it's not the first time the 79-year-old US president's health has come under scrutiny - here's a list of some of his biggest health scares and rumours:

‌



View 8 Images Trump even admitted to nodding off in a meeting with high-ranking military officials (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Bruised hands

Speculation surrounding Trump's health flared last year when photographs appeared to show mysterious red marks and bruising on his hands, which he appeared to try and conceal on at least one occasion with makeup.

In January, at a signing for his 'Board of Peace' with world leaders, Trump could once again be seen with a large blue bruise on his left hand - stretching from the knuckle of his middle finger right the way down to the base of his thumb.

‌



View 8 Images Trump's bruised hands have sparked frenzied speculation (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The White House announced in July that Trump had been diagnosed with chronic venous insufficiency, a condition which affects how veins pump blood to the heart.

Swollen ankles

Photographs of Trump in recent months have also appeared to show him with swollen ankles - suggesting he could be dealing with fluid retention. Some have pointed this out as potential evidence of cardiovascular strain or other age-related sickness - but his supporters claim the appearance of swelling is merely down to camera angles, or the cut of his trousers.

‌



View 8 Images The 79-year-old's ankles have appeared swollen in multiple recent public appearances (Image: AP)

Peeling scabs

Earlier this month, the President was spotted with a dark red patch on his neck during a Medal of Honour ceremony at the White House. After turning up over forty minutes late, Trump was also seen with discoloured hands whilst presenting the awards to military personnel.

‌



View 8 Images Trump's peeling scabs were attributed to a skin cream by his doctor

White House physician Sean Barbabella quickly addressed the speculation, explaining: "President Trump is using a very common cream on the right side of his neck, which is a preventative skin treatment, prescribed by the White House Doctor. The President is using this treatment for one week, and the redness is expected to last for a few weeks."

Facial paralysis

Rumours of Trump having suffered a stroke have been fuelled by signs of apparent drooping in his face. At an event honouring the victims of 9/11 in September, the US president's face appeared to fall on one side - prompting chatter on social media that he had either recently visited the dentist, or was potentially recovering from a TIA (transient ischemic attack), also known as a 'mini-stroke'.

‌



View 8 Images The US president's drooping face has led to rumours about a mini-stroke (Image: AP)

Slurring speech and forgetting words

Questions about the US President's cognitive health have been rife in his second term, with Trump appearing increasingly unfocused and rambling in major speeches as he approaches his 80s.

On Thursday, the 79-year-old slurred his words throughout an address to the American people giving an update on the Iran war, while a separate speech on transgender issues earlier this week saw him trailing off, repeating himself and struggling to complete sentences.

‌



View 8 Images Trump has seemed increasingly forgetful in his second term (Image: AP)

"Like there will be no trans.... mutilation," Trump said at one point in the speech, before adding: "We don't want any.... transgender gender mutilisation of our children."

Dementia fears

Having made political hay of Joe Biden's cognitive struggles into an issue at the 2024 election, Donald Trump's own grasp of current events and apparent memory have been called into question on multiple occasions.

‌



In a January 2026 press conference intended to celebrate his first year back in office, the US president veered off into a bizarre, rambling anecdote about a conversation with his mum during a childhood baseball game, before abruptly boasting about bringing back "insane asylums" to clear the streets.

And last month, during a meeting with Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi at the White House, a journalist asked Trump why he hadn't given US allies, such as Japan, any heads-up before launching the recent military strikes on Iran. He replied by turning to her and asking: "Why didn't you tell me about Pearl Harbor?"

View 8 Images The 79-year-old has fallen asleep in meetings (Image: X)

Article continues below

Trump also claimed he "aced" a "very difficult" cognitive exam, despite the paper he filled out being the MoCA a standard dementia test. He also appeared to misremember the animals he was asked to identify, recalling a question on a "lion, giraffe, fish, and a hippopotamus" - which the test's creator Dr Ziad Nasreddine later confirmed do not appear in any versions of the MoCA.

Falling asleep

Donald Trump has made a habit of falling asleep in meetings in his second term, even in front of the camera. On March 23, Trump struggled to stay awake during a law enforcement roundtable at the Memphis Air National Guard Base while officials praised his administration's crime-fighting efforts.

And just two weeks earlier, Trump reportedly admitted to supporters at a rally in Kentucky that he had fallen asleep during a planning meeting for military operations, jokingly noting he chose the name "Epic Fury" for an attack after waking up.

News.title: William and Kate lead the royals in huge show of unity as they celebrate Easter
News.content:
William and Kate lead the royals in huge show of unity as they celebrate Easter

The King and Queen have been joined by the Prince and Princess of Wales and their children, at the Easter Matins church service at St George’s Chapel, Windsor Castle, as they traditionally do each year

View 5 Images The Wales family on Easter Sunday (Image: Samir Hussein./WireImage)

The Prince and Princess of Wales and their children have joined a huge Royal Family gathering to celebrate Easter this morning.

‌



They were with the King and Queen who led the family in a major show of unity as they attended the Easter Sunday church service at St George’s Chapel, Windsor Castle, as they traditionally do each year.

‌



The Prince and Princess of Wales missed the service last year as they were spending the weekend with their children in Norfolk, and they were absent in 2024 as it came just over a week after Kate released an emotional video message disclosing that she had started a course of preventative chemotherapy following her cancer diagnosis.

‌



View 5 Images William and Kate with their three children lead the royals to church on Easter Sunday (Image: PA)

The outing also marks the biggest gathering of royals since the arrest of disgraced Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, with his daughters Princesses Beatrice and Eugenie skipping this morning's service. It emerged earlier this week that with the agreement of their uncle the King, the sisters have made alternative plans and will miss the family gathering.

William and Kate along with Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis walked out in front as they led the royals down the hill towards St George's Chapel in blustery conditions.

‌



Following them were Princess Anne and her husband Vice Admiral Sir Timothy Laurence as well Prince Edward and his son James, Viscount Severn.

5 View 5 Images Charlotte waves to those gathered near St George's Chapel (Image: PA) 5 View 5 Images Charlotte shares a sweet moment with dad William (Image: PA)

‌



Also among the royal party was Peter Phillips and his wife-to-be Harriet Sperling, who announced earlier this week they would be marrying in June. The Easter outing marks the first formal family event Harriet has appeared at, with her daughter Georgina joining Peter's daughters Savannah and Isla.

Charles and Camilla, dressed in a vibrant red coat, arrived by car and were greeted outside the chapel by their family before they headed inside for the service, with the King playfully tapping Louis on the shoulder as they went inside.

It comes as Beatice and Eugenie joined the Royal Family just three months ago for Christmas celebrations at Sandringham. Their invitation and acceptance was seen as a bold statement of support from the King who had sympathy for their plight.

‌



Since then, both women featured in the latest tranche of Epstein files released by the US State Department in January, while their father was arrest on suspicion of misconduct in public office amid the scandal surrounding his friendship with paedophile Jeffrey Epstein.

View 5 Images Peter Phillips and wife-to-be Harriet at Windsor Castle for the traditional Easter Sunday service (Image: PA)

While there is no suggestion at this stage that the King will strip them of their titles, those in royal circles suggest there is a “deep unease” about releasing any form of public statement regarding their princesses as allegations relating to the Epstein files continue to emerge.

‌



Last year both Andrew and Fergie joined the Easter service at Windsor, but neither attended due to their banishment from the Royal Family. The former Duke of York is expected to spent the day on the Sandringham estate, where he now lives and was seen walking his dogs yesterday. It is unclear how Fergie, who has not been seen in public since December, will be marking the occasion.

Royal Easter celebrations kicked off on Thursday when Charles distributed the traditional Royal Maundy gifts at a special service. He was joined by Camilla at St Asaph Cathedral in North Wales, where he gave out Maundy Money to to 77 men and 77 women who have showed outstanding Christian service and made a difference to the lives of people in their communities.

Article continues below

At that service, supporters with Union flags and Welsh flags lined the street outside the cathedral to greet the royal couple. However, protesters with yellow flags from Republic, an anti-monarchy campaign group, held a banner with the slogan “What are you hiding? Royal Epstein inquiry now”.

Hours before Charles and Camilla’s arrival, graffiti saying “Not our King” was also cleaned off a wall in the grounds of the building, which is the UK’s smallest ancient cathedral. The Easter service also comes days after Buckingham Palace announced Charles’ visit to the US will go ahead from April 27 to April 30 as planned, despite tensions between President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Keir Starmer over the Iran war.

News.title: 'Our daughter completed our family - hours after birth we got devastating news'
News.content:
'Our daughter completed our family - hours after birth we got devastating news'

Zoe Davies thought her family was complete when baby Madeline was born, but hours later doctors delivered devastating news. Now approaching her first birthday, 'Miracle Maddie' has defied all odds after emergency treatment at Great Ormond Street Hospital

View 8 Images Madeleine was supposed to complete her family - but just hours after her birth they were thrown into turmoil (Image: John Myers)

For Zoe Davies, her hospital visit to deliver her third daughter was meant to complete her family - but just hours after welcoming her daughter into the world, the family were given devastating news.

‌



Having experienced childbirth twice previously, the Ammanford mum understood what lay ahead, and the arrival of newborn Madeline at Glangwili Hospital in Carmarthen on 26 April last year through caesarean section had initially been welcomed by nursing staff as healthy and straightforward.

‌



Yet four hours afterwards, around midnight, the world of Zoe and partner Matthew Davies was thrown into turmoil. Medical staff delivered the devastating news to the pair that Madeline had suffered what was termed an "unexpected collapse" and her condition had become critical.

‌



View 8 Images Madeline arriving at Singleton Hospital in Swansea (Image: Zoe Davies)

Brit schoolboy's horror as he wakes up paralysed shattering pro boxing dreams READ MORE :

Madeline's oxygen saturation was "very low" while her temperature was described as "unmeasurable". Attempts were undertaken to stabilise her situation, but medical professionals determined she required an enhanced level of treatment only accessible at Singleton Hospital.

She was moved to the Swansea facility the next day, and it was there that Madeline's parents received the "horrific" revelation that she had been diagnosed with persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN), reports Wales Online. It is a severe life-threatening disorder where a newborn's pulmonary blood vessels fail to relax following delivery, hampering adequate oxygenation, resulting in critically low blood oxygen caused by elevated pressure within the lungs.

‌



View 8 Images Madeline pictured in the helicopter (Image: Zoe Davies)

Zoe, 27, said: "I began to notice things weren't right at Glangwili Hospital and I echoed my concerns to the midwife but unfortunately it got a bit dismissed. They didn't see any issues with Madeline at first but I felt things weren't quite right. I was trying to feed her and she was crying and choking.

"Unfortunately, by the time they noticed, it was quite severe and the oxygen had been starved from her brain for a little while. When we got to Singleton they were a bit more straight with us on how poorly she was, that she was very critical, and that we needed to prepare for the worst.

‌



View 8 Images Madeline breathing on her own with the equipment removed (Image: Zoe Davies)

"It was horrific. I was in bits – I was completely distraught. My partner and I couldn't even get our heads around what was happening, let alone what could happen – it was terrifying. Every time they were trying to get her to stabilise she wasn't responding.

"She was relying on the machines and every time they were trying to wean her off she was shutting down. They continued to do what they could and after a day they told us there was one final option – that she might be a candidate for a heart and lung bypass at Great Ormond Street Hospital in London."

‌



View 8 Images 'She has really shown her strength and courage,' said devoted mum Zoe (Image: John Myers)

At barely two days old, on April 28, Madeline was transported by air ambulance to the London hospital where she would spend the next 10 days. The trauma of her ordeal, combined with having to travel so soon after giving birth, took a severe toll on Zoe, who collapsed upon arriving in London, drifting in and out of consciousness before being rushed by blue-light ambulance to University College Hospital London, where she spent five days receiving IV treatment for sepsis.

Following her recovery, Zoe was discharged and finally reunited with Madeline and Matthew, who had been frantically shuttling between two hospitals, uncertain whether both his partner and newborn daughter would pull through. Zoe's father Paul made the journey to London to lend his support, while her mother remained in Ammanford caring for their two other daughters.

‌



View 8 Images Madeline arriving in London, pictured with her parents (Image: Zoe Davies)

At Great Ormond Street Hospital, doctors successfully stabilised Madeline, gradually reducing her medication before transferring her back to Singleton Hospital, where she spent a further four weeks in intensive care receiving the highest level of ventilation available. Yet, against all expectations, following four hospital admissions and countless procedures, machines, and medicines, Madeline was finally discharged on June 3.

‌



For two months after returning home, she required constant monitoring and medication every four hours, before her treatment was slowly reduced over the last nine months. With Madeline now rapidly approaching her first birthday, the family have had the chance to reflect on everything they have endured and conquered.

View 8 Images The Davies family reunited at Singleton Hospital in Swansea (Image: Zoe Davies)

"It's hard to believe what she's been through," Zoe said. "She was doing well throughout the whole pregnancy and there were no complications. We didn't know at the time if she was going to survive, and if she did what sort of life she would have, as oxygen had been starved from her brain.

‌



"We were terrified of what our life was going to look like. It just changed in a second, in an instant. We were just trying to stay positive at the time and keep talking to her and keep her pushing through and eventually she did. Since being home I've been through a lot of CBT therapy with the perinatal team after being diagnosed with post-traumatic stress after what happened. I was getting lots of flashbacks of all the events and how they unfolded. The images were stuck in my head for a long, long time. It has helped significantly."

View 8 Images 'Miracle Maddie' is now gearing up to turn one (Image: John Myers)

Ms Davies went on to say: "Madeline now has cardiology appointments on her heart and there's checks on her lungs and developmental things, if she's reaching her milestones and so on, which she is. I call her 'Miracle Maddie' – we all do in the family. We see what she went through, and how she overcame it, and she has become beyond what we ever imagined she would be – she has really shown her strength and courage.

Article continues below

"She's so strong-willed. Even in the hospital they said they couldn't believe how strong she was because she kept on trying to pull her tubes out as if to say: 'I'm fine'. From day one she was an absolute strength and even now she is just so busy and strong."

To mark Madeline's first birthday, Zoe expressed her desire to support Great Ormond Street Hospital and Singleton Hospital. She's organising a charity family fun day at Betws Rugby Club in Ammanford on April 25 and will also tackle the Three Peaks Challenge on May 16. Those wishing to contribute can do so by clicking here.

News.title: Flight declares mid-air emergency as fire erupts moments after Gatwick take-off
News.content:
Flight declares mid-air emergency as fire erupts moments after Gatwick take-off

TAP Air Portugal TP1329, bound for Porto, was forced to turn back to London Gatwick Airport after a fire erupted on board - with smoke seen pouring out of an overhead luggage compartment

View 2 Images The plane declared an emergency after taking off from Gatwick (Image: Getty)

A plane was forced to make a U-turn back to Gatwick Airport just minutes after take-off due to a fire erupting on board.

‌



Crew on TAP Air Portugal TP1329, bound for Porto, transmitted a Squawk 7700 - the international code for a general emergency - after detecting a "strong burning smell" and seeing smoke pouring out of an overhead luggage compartment.

‌



Passengers disembarked the plane at Gatwick, where emergency responders were waiting on the ground to carry out a technical assessment on the plane. Portuguese air and safety investigators later revealed the blaze had been sparked by an e-cigarette.

‌



The Lisbon-based Office for the Prevention and Investigation of Accidents in Civil Aviation and Rail said: "During the initial climb, before reaching 10,000ft, the cabin crew, who were in the rear of the aircraft, detected a strong burning smell and immediately informed the purser.

View 2 Images Flight-tracking data shows the plane performed a loop before landing at Gatwick (Image: AirNav Radar)

"He instructed them to contact the cockpit and reinforced the cabin crew in the area of the event. During this period, twelve passengers stood up and blocked the aisle.

‌



"A piece of hand luggage stowed in the overhead bin was found to be on fire, the cabin crew discharged a portable fire extinguisher and rapidly extinguished the flames, following which the smoke dissipated.

"The aircraft returned to London Gatwick Airport, after approximately 14 minutes of flight, for inspection. The firefighting team inspected the affected area, and the hand luggage was removed by firefighters for further investigation.

"The wellbeing of passengers and crew was confirmed, and a safety inspection was conducted before the flight to Porto. The cause of the fire was identified to be related to an electronic cigarette device that was inside the hand luggage."

Article continues below

Investigators also published a photo of the luggage the e-cigarette had been left in, showing the charred hole in its side that could have caused a disaster if it hadn't been for the quick-thinking of the crew on board.

The drama unfolded on February 8 but the results of a Portuguese investigation into the cause of the fire have only just been made public. It was not immediately clear how many passengers had been on board but the Airbus A320 jet can carry up to 180 people.

The flight eventually landed safely in Porto nearly three hours behind schedule after the plane was given the all-clear to head to Portugal.

News.title: DVLA cancels 33,000 driving licences over health condition as new tests announced
News.content:
DVLA cancels 33,000 driving licences over health condition as new tests announced

The DVLA has cancelled or refused to renew 32,944 driving licences over one specific health condition in - as the Government announces mandatory tests for drivers over 70

View 2 Images You must declare health conditions to the DVLA

Nearly 33,000 driving licences have been revoked by the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) due to particular medical issues. The driving authority took action to either withdraw or decline the renewal of licences amid fears that motorists might present a risk on Britain's roads.

‌



These instances related to vision-related ailments - and this development comes as the Government launches a clampdown on the matter amongst elderly drivers.

‌



The DVLA prohibited individuals from getting behind the wheel after learning of eyesight problems that could render drivers hazardous on the roads, reports Birmingham Live.

‌



A total of 32,944 such instances occurred over the past four years, according to freedom of information figures obtained by Marshall Motor Group. Motorists are required to inform the DVLA about any vision-related ailments that might affect their capacity to drive safely.

Fuel stations bracing for demand surge after Easter breaks amid 'shortage' threat READ MORE :

View 2 Images The DVLA has already refused to renew nearly 33,000 licences (Image: GETTY)

The Government has unveiled compulsory eyesight examinations for motorists aged over 70, following worries that existing regulations aren't sufficiently robust. Individuals must renew their driving licences upon reaching 70 and every three years thereafter.

‌



The stricter regulations could lead to additional driving licences being withdrawn. While it wasn't exclusively over-70s who had their licences removed because of their vision, the figures were considerably higher for this demographic.

The 70-79 age group recorded the greatest number of revoked licences - 10,794. A further 8,060 were recorded for those between 80 and 89, with 1,202 aged over 90.

Motoring expert Ben Welham from Marshall Motor Group warned: "Eyesight deterioration usually happens gradually, so drivers might not notice small changes over time."

‌



He went on to highlight the widespread nature of the issue: "The data shows this isn't limited to one age group, so maintaining good vision is relevant at every stage of life." Welham also stressed the importance of routine check-ups, saying: "Regular professional eye tests remain the safest way to make sure you meet the legal standard and can continue driving confidently."

He concluded with a key reminder for all motorists: "Drivers should be able to clearly read a standard number plate from 20 metres away."

Eyesight conditions aside, anyone with a specific health condition must inform the DVLA or risk facing a penalty. Penalties can potentially reach £1,000 for failing to comply. Drivers can check whether they need to inform the DVLA about their condition on Gov.uk and locate the forms or questionnaires they require. Separate forms for various conditions and disabilities are available, too. Get in touch with DVLA if you're unsure what steps to take.

News.title: Busted now after split - tragic health battle, rivals and thwarted reunion
News.content:
Busted now after split - tragic health battle, rivals and thwarted reunion

Busted rose to fame in 2002 with What I Go To School For before splitting in 2005 - the band reunited in March 2023 for a 20th anniversary tour

View 5 Images Busted formed in 2000 and split up in 2005 (Image: PA)

Busted devotees were left devastated when the pop-rock trio revealed their shock break up back in 2005 - though mercifully, it wasn't the final curtain for the band.

‌



James Bourne, Charlie Simpson and Matt Willis shot to stardom with their breakthrough track What I Go To School For in 2002, two years after they began, quickly snagging their maiden chart-topper with Year 3000 shortly afterwards. Yet despite their phenomenal achievements, the boy band called it quits just a few years down the line and pursued individual paths.

‌



Fast-forward to March 2023, they declared their official reunion with a 20th anniversary tour, which took place in 2025 - but what unfolded during those years in the wilderness? Each member experienced highs and lows, from wrestling with mental health crises and rehabilitation programmes, shock surgeries to 'extend life' to conquering the West End stage and launching McBusted.

‌



View 5 Images The band came back together in 2023 for a reunion tour (Image: Splash News)

James Bourne

Chief songwriter James grew up in Southend-on-Sea in Essex, where he met bandmate Matt Willis.

He relocated to the Big Apple following the 2005 split and launched a fresh pop-rock band dubbed Son Of Dork. The ensemble notched up a handful of top 10 singles before the members each branched out towards different ventures.

‌



James transformed their first album into a West End stage show in 2012, titled Loserville: The Musical. Come 2013, James and Matt revealed they were teaming up with McFly to create McBusted, embarking on a blockbuster two-year tour.

View 5 Images James was dating YouTuber Emily Canham (Image: Jeff Spicer/Getty Images)

Throughout his career, James has penned tracks for major acts such as The Saturdays, The Vamps and 5 Seconds of Summer. He dated YouTuber Emily Canham for four years, maintaining a discrete profile throughout, before they parted ways in November 2023.

‌



An insider revealed to The Sun: "James and Emily have called it quits and are each happily moving on with their lives. James has been non-stop with the tour and managing his time between the UK and his place in LA."

But now, aged 42, he has shared a devastating health update with fans. The musician was forced to quit his band's tour with McFly just hours before it kicked off due to his health.

Speaking on the first evening of the McFly vs Busted tour, bassist Matt Willis addressed his pal's absence, saying: "You may have noticed our best friend is not here tonight. James Bourne is really f***ing sick and we love him and we miss him.

‌



"This is the first show we've ever played without him and it's really weird but we're going to do the best we can. This happened really fast, y'know, health is wealth."

At the time, he was replaced by his brother Chris, who had appeared in the Year 3,000 video as a youngster.

Yesterday, James explained on social media he was awaiting major surgery which he hoped would "extend his life", adding that he was desperate to go back to making music and touring.

‌



While he has not disclosed the type of surgery, he wrote: "I realised it's been about six months since I posted last. I have a plan in place to have a major surgery that should extend my life and hopefully make me well enough to come back to what I love the most which is touring and making music. It really sucks to be out of the game. But there is hope!"

James released a statement before the tour began in 2023, explaining his absence from shows. "The VS tour kicks off tomorrow night in Birmingham and as excited as I've been all year for this tour to begin.

"I'm really sorry to say that over the last 8 days it has become clear that I am not in good enough health to play these shows." He didn't say what his health condition was and added that there was a lot of information he didn't have.

‌



"There's a lot of information I still don't have about my condition but my bandmates, management and I are unanimous in deciding that I should focus on medical stuff for now. I really hope I can be in a position to come back further down the line."

Matt Willis

View 5 Images Matt Willis paid tribute to his wife Emma on his rehabilitation journey (Image: PA)

Matt, 42, has battled alcohol and substance abuse throughout much of his adult years, entering rehabilitation on three separate occasions. He opened up about his struggles in 2023 in the BBC documentary, Matt Willis: Fighting Addiction, while paying tribute to his wife, Voice presenter Emma Willis, 50, for her unwavering support.

‌



"I dread to imagine where I'd be without her," he confessed, acknowledging he put her "through hell". The pair have three youngsters together, with Matt attributing his sobriety to becoming a father.

Throughout his life Matt says he would “get clean for a while” and then “start using again”. On his On The Mend podcast, Matt says it got to the point where he rang his drugs counsellor saying he doesn’t “want this anymore” and that he needs help.

The television personality also disclosed his previous deep involvement with The Church of Scientology, a faith embraced by Hollywood figures including Tom Cruise and John Travolta, though he ultimately severed connections.

‌



Matt claimed victory on I'm A Celebrity in 2006 before carving out an impressive West End portfolio, launching with Flashdance: The Musical in 2010. His stage credits extend to Footloose, Wicked, Little Shop of Horrors, Waitress and 2:22 A Ghost Story.

He and Emma also became the hosts of Love is Blind UK, bringing their own experience as a couple to the Netflix dating experiment, and have been the face of the UK branch of the show for a number of years.

Charlie Simpson

View 5 Images Charlie Simpson appeared on The Masked Singer

‌



Charlie made the decision to disband the group in 2005, stepping away from Busted to concentrate on his rock project, Fightstar. That is now on hiatus, but he's subsequently established his own record label.

Charlie tied the knot with Anna Barnard in 2014, and the pair welcomed two sons. But 2022 brought a frightening moment when their younger child, Jago, required emergency hospital treatment for 'secondary drowning' while the family were holidaying overseas.

"He spent the next three days in hospital and I'm so thankful for the amazing care he received. It was the worst thing we have ever experienced," Charlie revealed.

‌



In 2023, the musician made a television comeback, triumphing on The Masked Singer in the Rhino costume. "I was terrified the entire time. The thing I was scared most of was remembering lyrics. I often forget lyrics to my own songs on stage!" he admitted. Soon afterwards, Busted confirmed they were getting back together for a UK tour marking their 20th anniversary.

After bandmate James was forced to cancel his appearance, Charlie also sparked concern by cancelling his DJ sets last year. In emails sent to those who tried to buy tickets, he said: "Thank you so much for buy tickets to Charlie Simpson's DJ set at Gorilla Manchester.

"Unfortunately due to the ongoing health issues of James and the strain that it is putting on Charlie and the rest of the band, he has had to make the difficult decision to cancel all upcoming DJ sets."

Article continues below

Fans flocked to social media to share their worries. One wrote: "This feels really concerning. Hoping hard that James gets good health as soon as possible."

A second said: "It could just be that cos of the extra work that Matt and Charlie are picking up on the tour - it might not seem a lot to sing a few extra lines, but doing that every night along with anything else James might've done behind the scenes will take its toll." Another said they hoped it wasn't "bad news".

News.title: 'I worked for Royal Family - this is my worrying prediction for King Charles' state visit'
News.content:
'I worked for Royal Family - this is my worrying prediction for King Charles' state visit'

A former royal insider has raised concerns about potential challenges facing King Charles III during his upcoming state visit to the United States

View 3 Images Britain's King Charles III talks with US President Donald Trump (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

A former royal aide has warned that protests could overshadow King Charles III’s upcoming state visit to the United States. Ailsa Anderson, who previously served as press secretary to Queen Elizabeth II, said demonstrators could disrupt the diplomatic trip involving the King and Queen Camilla.

‌



The royal expert worked for the late monarch for several years and was responsible for handling communications and media strategy for the Royal Household, giving her extensive experience of how major royal visits are planned and managed.

‌



Speaking on The Royals podcast about the potential challenges facing palace officials, she said: “Well, obviously, as you've rightly said, the concerns are going to be protests, potentially by Epstein survivors, there of course is the Prince Harry and The Duchess of Sussex, dialogue surrounding them.

‌



“So we've already seen the King and the Queen and other members of the Royal Family heckled while carrying out official engagements in the UK. I haven't got a crystal ball, but I can almost predict there will be protests while they're there.

“This, of course, is going to take the shine off the work that they want to do and all that soft power, all that, trying to build back that special relationship between the US and the UK. What they don't want is a distraction, so that's all going to come into play.”

View 3 Images US President Donald Trump speaks to King Charles III (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The King is expected to travel to Washington DC later this month as part of a high-profile state visit hosted by President Donald Trump.

According to Buckingham Palace, the visit has been arranged on the advice of the British government and comes at the invitation of the US president. Officials say the trip will celebrate the longstanding ties between the United Kingdom and the United States, as the two nations mark the 250th anniversary of American independence.

The King and Queen are scheduled to travel to Washington DC and New York City, where a state dinner at the White House is planned and he is expected to address Congress.

‌



While Buckingham Palace initially confirmed only that the visit would take place in “late April”, President Trump later announced the dates publicly as April 27 to 29. A third stop is also expected to be included in the itinerary but has not yet been revealed.

After the main engagements conclude, the Queen is expected to return home while the King will continue to Bermuda for an additional visit.

View 3 Images The King and Queen with the US president and First Lady Melania (Image: PA)

‌



The trip comes at a diplomatically delicate moment following tensions between the US administration and the British government over the conflict in Iran.

However, political issues are not the only potential flashpoint. There have also been calls for the royal couple to meet victims linked to the late financier and convicted paedophile Jeffrey Epstein, who previously had ties to the King’s brother, Prince Andrew, Duke of York.

Democratic congressman Ro Khanna, who has campaigned for the release of Epstein-related files, has urged the King to meet survivors during the visit.

Article continues below

Palace officials have said such a meeting would not be possible, citing concerns that it could interfere with potential investigations in the UK. Andrew was arrested in February on suspicion of misconduct in public office but was later released without charge while the investigation continues. He has denied any wrongdoing.

The crew for Nasa's Artemis II mission have described seeing the far side of the Moon for the first time.

Nasa astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen have entered the third day of their mission on the Orion spacecraft that will carry them around the far side of the Moon and back to Earth.

"Something about you senses that is not the Moon that I'm used to seeing," Koch said.

The crew shared a photo they took of the Orientale basin of the Moon, which Nasa said marked "the first time the entire basin has been seen with human eyes".

As of 23:00 BST on Saturday, Nasa's online dashboard showed the Artemis II spacecraft was more than 180,000 miles (289,681km) from Earth.
